issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies an inventory class named "Stock" (with methods add/take/findStockIngredient/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock) and indicates SealSaloon should be associated with Stock. However, both template and solution implement that inventory functionality in a class named "Inventory", while "Stock.java" is present but empty. This conflicts with the specified design and can mislead students into implementing/modifying the wrong class name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make naming consistent across all artifacts: either rename Inventory to Stock (file/class name and all references) and remove the empty Stock.java, or update the problem statement/UML to use "Inventory" everywhere and explicitly remove/ignore Stock.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies SealSaloon has a (static) "stock" attribute of type "Stock". In the solution, the field is declared as "private static final Inventory stock" and the getter returns Inventory, contradicting the specified attribute type and association in the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: After choosing Stock vs Inventory naming, ensure SealSaloon.stock and its getter use the same type as the specification (e.g., "private static final Stock stock" and "public static Stock getStock()"). Alternatively, update the statement/UML to match Inventory if that is the intended type.
